notes: The repeated going down, Tarshish, and flight from the LORD’s presence are deliberate narrative features. “Hurled” links the wind, cargo, and Jonah’s later casting into the sea.
The creature is a “great fish,” without a species identification. The three days and three nights are retained as stated. This verse is 2:1 in the Hebrew source.
vocabulary: Objects used to make a selection; the sailors use them here to seek the cause of the disaster.
The repeated word moves from terror in the storm to fear directed toward the LORD.

notes: Verse 4 can be heard as confidence about looking again or as a question. “Their faithful love” in verse 8 may mean loyalty they abandon or kindness available to them; the possessive is retained.
vocabulary: The realm of the dead; the prayer describes the threat of death through its belly and the earth’s bars.
Rescue; the closing line assigns it to the LORD.

notes: “Great before God” preserves the Hebrew phrase, also understood as “exceedingly great.” The three-day journey is not explained as a circumference or a precise city diameter. “Overturned” can describe destruction or a reversal of condition.
The king says “Who knows?” God’s response is then connected with the people’s deeds and turning from violence. Raah appears as both evil conduct and threatened disaster.
vocabulary: Coarse cloth worn in mourning or humbling oneself.
Both are included in the decree’s fasting and sackcloth; the unusual animal participation remains explicit.

notes: Jonah regards the spared city as a “great wrong.” The wording echoes the book’s evil/disaster vocabulary; it expresses Jonah’s complaint, not the narrator’s endorsement.

The anger question may concern its rightness or intensity. The plant’s species and the rare adjective for the east wind are uncertain; the draft does not specify a castor plant or gourd as settled fact.

The right-hand/left-hand description may concern children or a broader lack of discernment; the text says people, not explicitly infants. It gives more than 120,000 and ends with many animals and an unanswered question.
vocabulary: The same verb links fish, plant, worm, and wind as agents in the story.
The repeated concern for plant and city carries the final comparison.
